comments.text:
I used to be a twice a month barber client. Shapeup was $15 and I tip $4-5. I could also just text and pull up. Now, some barbers want you to download an app, pay a deposit and some are charging $30-$60 just for a shapeup. I also have long hair so pre-c0vid I was able to get my hair braided $45-$65) plus get a shapeup ($15) for under $100. I could tip both my braider and barber and still have money let for something to eat. The celebrity barbers messed everything up bragging about $100 haircuts. I know barbers that hiked their prices overnight.

Fortunately for me I am mainly remote and I can where a hat when I go to the office so I can make my cuts stretch. The same barber who hiked up his prices and I stopped going saw me out and begged me to come back and he would go back to his original prices. The barbers/stylists got too greedy. I totally get them wanting appointments to have a workable schedule but some of them got too outrageous. I know cats who went bald or learned how to cut their own hair from YouTube. The second dude has the right mentality. Go out and hustle to get your clientele up and let the people help you bring in heads.

comments.author: @AbrahamJankans
comments.text: Barbers and barbershops need to start thinking like sophisticated business. Concepts like product market fit and ICP (Ideal Customer Profile), share of wallet are very applicable. I see barbers cutting kids hair, then a professional then a college student. These are all different customers at different price points. The more experienced barbers should focus on the higher value customers like professionals, while the entry level barbers should do the kids cuts. Also, dollars per sitting, or how much money per seat per half hour. Professionals who are busy and will pay more for the convenience, and add on services. Lastly, there needs to be some consolidation in the market. Supercuts and sports clips have done a good job providing a consistent service. I think the barber industry has a lot of innovation and improvement that could unlock a lot of value.
